slides.say: It is known that a region suits people better the higher the percent of carbon in its soil, and the lower the percent of hydrogen. On which planet is the region that suits people best?

slides: So the question gives us a rule. More carbon is better, and less hydrogen is better. We want the sample with both.
Do we check the exact numbers of every sample? No. We solve it by understanding, with our eyes.

slides.say: More carbon means further to the right, because carbon goes across.
Less hydrogen means lower down, because hydrogen goes up.
So we want a sample that is both on the right and at the bottom. That's the bottom right corner.
Who's in the corner? The ring at about seventy-four percent carbon and three percent hydrogen. It has more carbon than every other sample, and less hydrogen than all of them.

slides: The key says a ring is Neptune.

slides.say: What about Mercury? It has samples far to the right too. But look how high they are. They have a lot of hydrogen, so they don't suit people.
Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
